bimba:
[Vamu+ba]  CL=8 “mana + va (Moggallāna . 7.122; Dhān. Ṭīkā 53, 529).
vī + van. When the letter ‘mum’ is added to the root, when mu and na are elided, it becomes ‘vīva’.
By shortening (vowel contraction) and changing v to b, the form ‘bimba’ is produced (according to the Thoma).
Additionally, another meaning ‘that which is pleasing or delightful’ may be included.”
(1) The body; the physical self (attabhāva)
 (2) Image; statue; figure; picture/photograph
 (3) Circle; disk; orb (such as the moon or sun)
 (4) The bimba fruit
(5) The bimba tree
“See also: Bimboṭṭha).”
